# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey. I can feel the button and three wires, but I don't know their colors or what the manual says. I need to wait for information from Mute (who reads the manual) relayed through Deaf, or directly from Mute since Mute speaks to me.

I have nothing to report yet and no instructions received. I should wait and let Mute and Deaf establish communication first, since I go last in turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf) - meaning I actually act *before* Deaf speaks this round, but *after* Mute. Let me check if Mute sent anything... nothing shown yet in my context.

I'll wait this turn since I have no information to act on and nothing useful to send yet.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display shows 0. Light is green. There is a large button labeled push to defeat. Wires from left to right are green, yellow, red.

Deaf has told me the display shows 0, light is green, button is labeled "push to defeat", and wires left to right are green, yellow, red. This is useful physical/visual info, but I still need the manual (Mute) to know what these mean - what to do given a green light, 0 display, and this wire order/colors.

I should pass this visual information to Mute, since Mute can't see the bomb but can read the manual and match conditions. I'll relay what Deaf told me to Mute so they can cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is green, button labeled push to defeat, wires left to right are green, yellow, red. What does the manual say to do?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is gesturing to me. I think it means wire 2, which is yellow. My best guess is Mute wants you to cut the yellow wire. Wait for confirmation before acting if possible.

Deaf saw a gesture from Mute pointing to wire 2 (yellow), and interprets it as an instruction to cut the yellow wire. But I should be careful - this is Deaf's guess about what the gesture meant, not a direct confirmation from Mute via speech. Since Mute cannot speak but I can hear Mute's speech... wait, Mute "cannot speak" - let me recheck. Mute reads manual but cannot speak. So Mute communicates only via gesture, which reaches Deaf and me (Blind) - wait, my channels say "when you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's about MY gestures. Let me check what Mute's gestures do - gestures go to whoever can see: Deaf can see, I (Blind) cannot see gestures at all ("Blind: cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed").

So I never receive Mute's gestures directly - only Deaf can see them. This matches: Deaf relayed the interpretation to me. This is the only path since Mute cannot speak.

I should ask Deaf to confirm more precisely, or ask Mute (via Deaf?) - but I can't speak to Deaf... wait, I can! Let me check: "When you speak, Mute receives it." "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." So my speech only goes to Mute, not Deaf. My gesture goes to both Deaf and Mute.

I should gesture to Deaf to ask for confirmation, but gestures are just symbols - I can't ask questions meaningfully. Better: I should proceed cautiously. Given the manual is only readable by Mute, and Mute's only way to communicate is gesture (seen by Deaf), Deaf's relay is our best information. Wire 2 = yellow. Let's ask Deaf to get more confirmation before I cut, since a wrong cut could be fatal.

I'll wait one more turn and gesture something simple to acknowledge, but I have no way to ask Deaf without gesture (which only carries symbols, not real questions). Actually I can gesture to Deaf - Deaf receives gestures. But gestures are just abstract symbols without pre-agreed meaning. Since this is turn 3 and the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - my message now goes to Deaf (via gesture) and Mute (via speech), and Deaf will speak after me this round, so if I ask Deaf now, they can respond in their turn.

I'll gesture to Deaf using a "wait/confirm" style, but simplest: use speak isn't received by Deaf. Only gesture reaches Deaf. Let me send a gesture asking for confirmation - though gestures have no inherent meaning, I can establish a convention: ✋ (stop/wait) then 👆 (point, meaning "wire 2?"). Actually establishing conventions on the fly is exactly what we must do.

I'll gesture to Deaf: 👆✌ (point + two fingers) meaning "wire 2?" and wait for their confirmation before cutting.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed, I believe the instruction is to cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Mute repeated a stop gesture alone, which I read as confirmation. Proceed with wire 2 if you are ready.

Deaf has now confirmed twice - both from Mute's gesture pointing at wire 2/yellow, and Mute's repeated gesture read as confirmation. This is consistent with two independent readings from Deaf. Given the constraints of our communication (Mute can only gesture, Deaf sees gestures and relays via speech to me), this is as much confirmation as we can reasonably get.

I'll proceed with cutting wire 2 (the yellow wire), since this matches the physical wire position Deaf described earlier (left to right: green, yellow, red — so wire 2 is yellow).

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
